projects.name: Chattrix
projects.description: A full-stack real-time one-to-one chat application built with Node.js, Express, MongoDB, EJS, and Socket.IO. It includes secure JWT cookie authentication, instant messaging, image uploads, user search, admin management, and responsive UI.
features: Secure email or mobile login with cookie-based JWT authentication
Real-time one-to-one messaging using Socket.IO
Search users by name, email, or Bangladeshi mobile number
Send text messages and up to five image attachments per message
Create and delete conversations with message history
Admin-only user management panel
Avatar upload and validation support
Responsive EJS-based UI with toast notifications

dataSource.notes: User data, conversations, and messages are stored in MongoDB using Mongoose models.

stateManagement.persistence: Messages and conversation data are stored in MongoDB and synced in real time across connected clients.

projectStructure.public/: Static assets, styles, and uploaded user files

projects.name: CommonGround
projects.category: Community Volunteering and Social Events Management Platform
projects.description: A full-stack community volunteering platform designed to connect event organizers with volunteers. CommonGround enables organizers to create, manage, and monitor volunteering events while allowing participants to discover upcoming opportunities, join events, track their participation, and contribute to community development. The platform includes event capacity management, secure authentication, participant tracking, and responsive interfaces with dark and light themes.
features: Responsive landing page with hero banner, statistics, recent events carousel, gallery, and newsletter section
Browse upcoming volunteering events filtered by date and Asia/Dhaka timezone
Detailed event pages displaying event information, organizer details, and volunteer capacity
Create volunteering events with rich-text descriptions, image thumbnails, dates, locations, and categories
Edit and delete events created by organizers
Join volunteering events with real-time volunteer capacity validation
Prevent duplicate event registrations
Concurrency-safe volunteer slot reservation to prevent event overbooking
Dedicated joined events section for participants
Leave previously joined events and release reserved volunteer slots
Dedicated event management dashboard for organizers
Role-oriented event management for organizers and participants
Email/password authentication using Better Auth
Google OAuth authentication
JWT-based authentication for protected backend API endpoints
Remote JWKS-based JWT verification using jose
Secure authorization using Bearer tokens
Automatic synchronization of event information with participant join records
Upcoming events listing sorted by nearest event date
Homepage displaying the six nearest upcoming events
Dark and light theme with preference persisted in localStorage
Toast notifications for success and error feedback
Client-side form validation
MongoDB database integration for event and participant management
Serverless backend deployment using Vercel

dataSource.notes: The frontend uses MongoDB through Better Auth for authentication data. Event and joined-event data are managed by the Express backend using the official MongoDB Node.js driver. The primary database name is CommonGround.

stateManagement.persistence: Event and participation data are persisted through the backend REST API and MongoDB. Authentication sessions are managed by Better Auth, with JWT tokens used for authorized backend API requests. Dark and light theme preferences are persisted using localStorage.

Frontend.src/app/: Next.js App Router pages for the landing page, event listing, event details, event creation, event editing, joined events, event management, and authentication
Frontend.src/components/: Reusable UI components, forms, event cards, navigation, providers, and other interface components
Frontend.src/lib/: Better Auth configuration, browser authentication client, JWT token utilities, and API-related helpers
Frontend.public/: Static assets, gallery images, and application resources

Backend.API: Express 5 REST API with event management, participant registration, and organizer event endpoints
Backend.Database: MongoDB using the official MongoDB Node.js driver
Backend.Authentication: Better Auth JWT verification using jose and remote JWKS
Backend.Middleware: JWT verification, CORS, and request processing
Backend.Deployment: Serverless Express application hosted on Vercel

projects.name: LearnTest
projects.category: Learning Management and Online Assessment Platform
projects.description: An AI-assisted full-stack learning management and assessment platform developed for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon. LearnTest connects students with educational content, allowing them to explore videos, questions, playlists, and exams while enabling teachers to create learning materials, evaluate students, manage content, and generate earnings.
features: Role-based authentication system supporting Students, Teachers, and Admins
Email/password authentication with email verification and password reset
Social authentication using Google and GitHub
Dedicated student dashboard for managing personal learning activities
Browse and discover educational videos, questions, playlists, and exams
Watch educational videos with authorization support
Take online examinations, submit assignments, and view grades and feedback
Bookmark learning content and follow favorite teachers
Purchase premium educational content
Teacher Studio dashboard for content and earnings management
Create and manage educational videos, questions, exams, and playlists
Review and grade student examination submissions
Teacher analytics for views, earnings, and student engagement
Set prices for premium educational content
Admin dashboard for user management and role management
Content moderation, transaction monitoring, and platform analytics
Teacher payout management and administrative audit logs

dataSource.notes: Application data is managed through the backend API and MongoDB using Mongoose.

stateManagement.persistence: Application data is persisted through the backend REST API and MongoDB. Authentication sessions are managed by Better Auth using secure HttpOnly cookies.

Frontend.app/: Next.js App Router pages for authentication, student dashboard, teacher studio, and admin panel
Frontend.components/: Reusable UI components, cards, dialogs, and video player
Frontend.lib/: API client, authentication context, custom hooks, TypeScript types, and validation utilities

projects.name: বাজার দর (BazarDor)
projects.description: A responsive Bangla market-price web application that helps users explore everyday product prices, compare market rates, and see price changes at a glance. It supports mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts and presents prices using Bengali numerals.
projects.tagline: বাজার দর — প্রয়োজনীয় পণ্যের দাম এক নজরে।
features: Responsive layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop
Home-page sections for products whose prices have increased or decreased, plus the full product list
Product cards showing illustrations, Bengali names, units, current prices, and percentage changes
Product details with minimum, maximum, and average prices and market-wise prices
Category-based product browsing
Sorting by default order, lowest price, or highest price
Bengali numeral formatting for prices
Email/password registration and sign-in
Google and GitHub social sign-in when configured
Protected pages for authenticated users where required
Profile viewing and name updates
Toast notifications for authentication, validation, and other actions
Loading skeletons while data is fetched
Friendly not-found handling for invalid routes or missing products and categories
SEO page titles and descriptions through Next.js metadata
notes: The README lists ATL_API and DATABASE_URL as environment-variable examples; the actual service and database engine are not specified there.
Displayed prices are indicative and may vary depending on the market and current conditions.
OAuth credentials, database credentials, and other secrets should be configured in environment variables and must not be committed to the repository.
